difference.rationale: Published Oxc follows ES chained-label continue semantics, while pinned QuickJS only makes the label immediately attached to a loop continuable; the Rust compiler deliberately preserves the Oxc semantic result.

Pinned QuickJS rejects an instance field named `prototype`, a check its own source marks `XXX: spec: not consistent with method name checks` (quickjs.c:25394). ECMAScript only reserves `constructor` for instance fields and `prototype` for static ones, and V8 accepts the fixture, so the frontend follows the specification.

Pinned QuickJS caps parser recursion around 695 nested parentheses and reports `stack overflow`; the Oxc front end parses the same source on its isolated 64 MiB frontend stack. The bounded depth is a QuickJS resource limit rather than ECMAScript grammar, so the frontend keeps accepting well-formed deeply nested sources.
The Oxc front end owns RegExp literal boundaries and flags, while QuickJS-compatible pattern parsing is deliberately delegated to the future RegExp layer.
